Nondominium × Commitment Pooling: what v0.1 must ship

Source: the "Nondominium × Commitment Pooling" proposal (Grassroots Economics), pasted 2026-10-06. Goal of this round: isolate the features this use case actually needs, and draw a release boundary tight enough to ship something clear, useful and valuable.

The proposal's own test is three questions: can a pool use persistent Nondominium identities without losing its simplicity, can fulfillment emit Valueflows events that change the state of a real object, and does that information improve pooling, settlement or provenance. An MVP is the smallest thing that answers all three on one real case.

Nondominium grounds the commitment.
The pool stays theirs.The MVP is the half CPP lacks: a persistent object, a commitment pointing at it, a validated event that changes its state, and a receipt a pool can cite. Curation, valuation, limits and swaps stay in Sarafu.

1What the proposal asks for

The proposal's chain is Agent → Resource → Process → Commitment → Pool → Economic Event → Validated State Change. Read against the code, most links already exist as data; what is missing is the path a person walks through them.

already worksmodel to copyidearisk
Repair example is our best fitRepairer identity, machine identity, commitment, NeedsRepair → repair → Operational, validation, fulfillment, settlement.Every noun maps to something we already model: Physical NDO, EconomicResource, Commitment, EconomicEvent, Claim, InMaintenance.
CPP has four functionsCuration, Valuation, Limitation, Exchange (Swap Limiter, Value Index, Treasury), live on Sarafu.Network.None of the four is Nondominium's job in v0.1. Reimplementing them would be a second, worse Sarafu.
The strongest phrase"Persistent economic identity and objects" is what separates Layer 0 from yet another accounting or currency system.The demo must make the machine's identity outlive the commitment: same NDO before, during and after, with its history attached.
The proposal says reciprocal"When does a collection of resources and commitments become an actual pool with joint consequences?" is asked of Nondominium.A fair question for v0.2+, not a v0.1 feature. Record it, do not build it.
Tomatoes are the weak example100 kg of tomatoes is a consumable: quantity, not identity. A pool already handles it fine without us.It does not exercise Layer 0. Keep it out of the first case.

3Against the prototypes and Tibi's Perspectives

Read 2026-10-06: the six v0.1 directions in nondominium-design-system (src/lib/prototypes/directions.ts, shared store src/lib/prototypes/store/), and Tibi's Perspectives in documentation/requirements/ui_design.md and ui_architecture.md §16 (commits 92c69f5, 38f9fc8, d91fe28, 2026-09-30). No direction is chosen yet: all six are candidate.

already worksmodel to copyidearisk
D and F are the demoD shows the pool's view of need; F shows the same facts as VF entries per conductor.Whichever direction wins, these two views are what to show GE.
The voucher flows the other wayCPP: the repairer issues a voucher ("I will do 5 repairs"), the requester holds and redeems it.Redemption is the moment a Commitment on a specific machine is born. The receipt then proves the voucher was honoured on that object.
The slice is a Work Perspective seedOpening, taking and fulfilling a repair is exactly "what do I engage in today"; the machine with its Repair agent is the Resource Perspective.Building it as a thin first Work Perspective avoids building it twice.
The Intent gap is realValueflows: an Intent is a want or offer with one side open; a Commitment has both provider and receiver. "Tractor needs repair, who can do it?" is an Intent.Card 5's lean (needs-repair derived from an open commitment) only holds if the requester names the repairer up front.
decided

1. How is an unassigned repair request modelled?

Prototypes and zome_gouvernance only have Commitment, which names both provider and receiver. A breakdown with no repairer yet is a Valueflows Intent, which Nondominium does not implement.

★ my lean, because It matches CPP's real flow (redeem a specific repairer's voucher) and keeps v0.1 schema-free; Intent becomes the v0.2 step for open calls.

decided

2. Where does the slice's UI live?

ui_design.md § Perspectives ToDos makes the Perspective switcher the next UI work; today's shell is Lobby → Group → NDO with no commitment screens.

★ my lean, because The repair loop is the first concrete content Work and Resource Perspectives can carry, so the work counts twice.

decided

3. Choose the target direction before or after the slice?

All six directions (A Mycelium to F Flow Graph) are candidate; issue #147 wants design-system improvements in the app before v0.1.0.

★ my lean, because A real scenario is a better selection criterion than taste, and it needs no new code: the shared store already mocks the loop.

4The repair case, end to end

One machine, one repairer, one requester, one pool. The large box is Nondominium; the small one is the pool on Sarafu, out of scope.

5In, out, and the line between

The release boundary as I would draw it. The cards below decide the contested items.

6Decisions waiting on you

Ten calls (three more in the prototypes zone). Card 1 frames the rest: if the slice goes into v0.1.0 itself, the release date moves.

decided

4. Where does the repair slice ship?

Milestone "v0.1.0 peer-mesh" (#123) is Lobby + Group + NDO Layer 0 and lists economic processes as OUT. This use case needs commitments, events and claims in the UI, roughly #141 plus three new screens.

★ my lean, because peer-mesh is nearly done and is the substrate the slice stands on. A separate milestone gives GE a release that is about their case, with nothing else in its notes.

decided

5. Which Grassroots Economics case?

The proposal lists repair, agricultural, transport or service pools. The choice decides which existing primitives get exercised.

★ my lean, because It is the proposal's own worked example and the one where persistent identity visibly matters. Confirm with GE that a real repair pool exists, in a note.

decided

6. How much of the pool lives in Nondominium?

CPP's four functions (curation, valuation, limitation, exchange) run on Sarafu. Something must make the pool visible in the demo.

★ my lean, because It answers question 3 of the proposal visually (does our info improve pooling?) without a single pool rule living here.

decided

7. How does a pool reference our objects?

The integration contract is the receipt: what Sarafu (or a human curator) holds that points back into Nondominium.

★ my lean, because The receipt is the one artefact both sides can test against, and Valueflows is the common language the proposal names.

decided

8. How is "needs repair" represented?

OperationalState has Available, Reserved, InTransit, InStorage, InMaintenance, InUse, PendingValidation (crates/shared/src/types.rs). No NeedsRepair, and OperationalState means "the process acting on it", not condition.

★ my lean, because The commitment already says the machine needs repair; deriving it keeps the data model untouched for v0.1.

decided

9. Who validates that the repair happened?

The proposal leans on peer validation. ValidationReceipt and ResourceValidation exist, partly stubbed.

★ my lean, because One witness is the smallest thing that is honestly peer validation rather than a two-party handshake, and it uses an entry that exists.

decided

10. PPRs in the slice?

MaintenanceFulfillmentCompleted is one of the 16 PPR categories, but issuance inserts a placeholder counterparty signature and claims are DHT-linked despite the privacy goal.

★ my lean, because Shipping known-weak signatures in the first external demo would cost more trust than the feature earns.

decided

11. Who may accept a repair commitment?

Specialized role validation (#34) auto-approves today; the Repair role exists in zome_person, which is not in the NDO cell.

★ my lean, because Gating adds work and no evidence for the three proposal questions.

decided

12. Do write paths go through evaluate_state_transition?

Issue #145 is open: propose_commitment and log_economic_event write directly; the operator is advisory.

★ my lean, because #145 is a design decision of its own; the slice should not decide it by accident.

decided

13. Where do commitments and events live?

Each NDO cell has zome_gouvernance, so the machine's commitments can sit in the machine's own DHT. The shared nondominium cell and hREA are alternatives.

★ my lean, because It is the literal claim of the proposal: events accumulate around the persistent object.

7What done looks like

The slice is done when a demo answers the proposal's three questions on two physical machines, without a sentence of hand-waving.

already worksidea
Q1, simplicity keptA GE curator creates nothing in Nondominium beyond pasting a link or loading a receipt.Falsifier: any step requires a pool operator to learn our data model.
Q2, fulfillment changes the objectAfter the Claim, the machine's NDO shows the repair in its history and its resource is Available again, seen from the other machine.Falsifier: the state or history differs between the two peers after sync.
Q3, information improves poolingThe Group's pool view shows which machines are down and which commitments are open; the receipt names validators.Ask GE directly whether this changes a curation or settlement decision. Their answer is the result.
